primitives.name: Visual Contrast Duality
primitives.verbatim_quote: **This is the real finding, and it is a measured number, not a count.** Every cockpit card shell is `border-titanium/40` on `bg-eclipse/40` (or `/70`, or bare).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C': 'contrast ratio dimensionless', 'L1': 'lightness of foreground color (0-1)', 'L2': 'lightness of background color (0-1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Color space is perceptually uniform; lightness values are normalized to [0,1]; contrast ratio is computed using standard luminance formula.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When $\Delta C < 0.05$, visual separation becomes indistinguishable.

layer2.mapping: Token color pairs map to binary compliance states in GSI's Bayesian model; each pair defines a contrast boundary in the UI state space.
layer2.telemetry: Observed contrast ratio per card shell across 60 files.

primitives.name: Role-Based Color Assignment
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## F2 (medium) — TWO ACTION BUTTONS WEAR STATE COLOURS.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R(b)': 'role assignment function for button b', 'B_action': 'set of action buttons'}
primitives.assumptions: Buttons are categorized based on semantic role; color assignments are consistent with design token vocabulary.

layer2.mapping: GSE evaluates button roles against token system; mismatch triggers alert state in UI rendering kernel.
layer2.telemetry: Button color usage vs. semantic role mapping across cockpit components.

primitives.name: Layout Overflow Signal
primitives.verbatim_quote: Read strictly, the token system declares `verify`/`alert` as `[STATE]` and `plasma` as the sole `[ACTION]`, so these two are off-role by the repo's own vocabulary.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'O(T)': 'overflow indicator for text element T', 'T': 'textual content with truncation', 'constraint(t)': 'bounding width of container'}
primitives.assumptions: Text elements are subject to bounded containers; overflow occurs when content exceeds bounds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When $\mathcal{O}(T) = 1$, layout instability may occur during rendering.

layer2.mapping: GSE monitors truncation signals; triggers layout adjustment upon overflow detection.
layer2.telemetry: Number of truncated elements per page with bounding box metrics.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that visual QA operates under a dual constraint: contrast and semantic clarity. The first primitive establishes a mathematical framework for measuring visual separation between adjacent UI elements through contrast ratios. When two colors are too similar (e.g., titanium/40 on eclipse/40), they fail the WCAG threshold, creating a perceptual barrier. The second primitive models how color roles must align with semantic intent—buttons should not adopt state colors unless their behavior is truly stateful. The third primitive addresses layout stability, where unbounded text elements cause overflow issues that affect readability and spacing. Each primitive contributes to a unified signal processing pipeline where inputs are UI tokens, transformations are semantic and perceptual checks, and outputs are binary compliance verdicts. Failure modes arise when these checks are bypassed or misapplied, leading to degraded UX or accessibility violations.
